title: Commit envelope router and kernel-aware prober for early-token acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We want to improve speculative decoding reliability and unit economics by making early-accept decisions (commit) based on a bounded confidence envelope computed from prefill probes and kernel cost estimates. Current speculative flows either accept too eagerly (leading to rollbacks and user-visible artifacts) or too conservatively (missing latency wins). This ticket proposes a new runtime component: the Commit Envelope Router (CER) plus a Kernel-Aware Prober (KAP).
detailed_proposal: 1) Commit Envelope Router (CER): CER maintains a short-lived confidence envelope per request derived from: (a) prefill partial outputs (probability mass or logit deltas), (b) per-model historical acceptance curves, and (c) kernel-cost signals (estimated additional decode latency if routed to a given kernel). CER produces: accept/confidence score + an allowed rollback window (number of tokens).
kernel_prober_description: 2) Kernel-Aware Prober (KAP): lightweight microbench harness that runs short synthetic prefill probes (prefill-length 8-32 tokens) against candidate model+kernel pairs to measure per-request latency delta and token-cost delta. KAP's outputs feed CER to bias routing toward fast kernels when confidence margins are tight.
fallback_strategy: 3) Fallbacks: when CER acceptance falls below threshold or rollback budget is exceeded we route to a safe, high-coverage path: (a) full-prefill on verified kernel, (b) slower but verified model variant, or (c) canonical hosted model. We add a fast rollback path where partial tokens are suppressed and a full re-decode is triggered with tracing for postmortem.
acceptance_metrics: Key metrics: early_accept_rate, false_accept_rate (cases needing rollback), rollback_latency_penalty, end-to-end P50/P95 latency change, cost_per_1000_tokens, acceptance_coverage_by_model, per-kernel rollback rate. Targets: false_accept_rate < 0.8%, rollback_latency_penalty < 40ms median, end-to-end P95 latency improved by >=8% for targeted workloads.
testing_and_experiments: Experiment plan: phase A synthetic workloads (deterministic prompts) to validate calibration; phase B internal canary on low-traffic orgs; phase C progressive ramp with traffic shaping. Tests: unit tests for envelope math, fuzz tests for edge cases (high-entropy prompts), integration tests for end-to-end rollback, chaos test simulating kernel OOM and network partition.
observability: Add CER/KAP spans to trace (request-level), new dashboard slices: envelope width distribution, per-model acceptance heatmap, rollback reasons distribution, kernel-probe latency histogram. Emit sample payloads to debugging bucket for incidents (PII scrubbed).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gated implementation. 2) Canary 1% of hosted traffic with conservative thresholds. 3) Expand to Dedicated with opt-in via config. 4) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, flip default for low-latency routes. 5) Full rollout only after post-canary review and infra scaling assessment.
operational_runbook: If rollback rate > 2% for 1h: (a) disable CER globally, (b) force all routes to safe-path; (c) page on-call runtime infra; (d) collect sample traces and kernel probe logs; (e) revert to previous thresholds while we investigate.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary shows false_accept_rate < 0.8% and P95 latency improvement >= 8% on targeted SLA routes
Kernel prober overhead < 1.5ms p50 and < 5ms p95 on average across regions
Telemetry: envelope width, acceptance decisions, and rollback reasons are available in Console with 48h retention for canary runs
Automated regression tests covering rollback trigger, safe-path routing, and kernel-prober failures
Security review completed and KMS usage for any sample payloads stored in debug bucket
